cases.title: Added HandleContext to re-enter soft-rewritten Requests. (#709)
cases.bug: HandleContext resets the context (handlers and index) and re-enters routing without restoring them, so the original chain continues on the new route's handlers and middleware re-runs; it also returns c to the pool while still in use

matched.title: HandleContext puts the context back in the pool a second time
matched.failure: A handler calls `c.Request.URL.Path = "/other"; engine.HandleContext(c)`. The context is Put once inside HandleContext, then again by ServeHTTP. The pool now holds the same pointer twice. Two concurrent requests can each Get the same *Context and overwrite each other's Request, Params, Keys and writer. The result is cross-request data leaks and corrupted responses. If another request takes c from the pool between the first Put and the end of the outer handler, it is also shared with the still-ru
notes: removed evidence that does not resolve: ref:gin.go:265

matched.title: reset() in the middle of an in-flight chain discards request state
matched.failure: A middleware stores `c.Set("user", u)`, and a later handler calls `HandleContext`. Handlers in the re-entered chain no longer see "user". After `HandleContext` returns, the outer chain's `c.Next()` loop continues from the re-entered chain's index. It may re-run handlers or skip the rest of the chain, and the outer middleware can see an inconsistent `c.index`.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading did not confirm the failing case (Calling reset() is how HandleContext re-enters the request from a clean state. Losing Keys and the old chain's index is what re-entry means. The pool double-Put is already covered by finding 0.)

matched.title: c.reset() wipes the context state and the doc comment names a field that does not exist
matched.failure: A caller who follows the comment and writes c.Request.Path = "/new" gets a compile error. A caller who sets URL.Path and calls HandleContext loses the Keys set by earlier middleware. Their later code then sees an empty Keys map and index state that was reset underneath it.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading did not confirm the failing case (The comment says c.Request.Path where it should say c.Request.URL.Path, which is a documentation slip with no effect on behaviour. The state reset is intended re-entry behaviour.)
